Some core Gaia instrument and pipeline stage names shall stay exact.

If the required inputs are not fully available, the simulator shall stop and mark the run as incomplete rather than producing something that appears finished.
For downstream handoff, the system shall export only outputs that pass the expected format checks.
The system shall tell the user exactly what is missing or mismatched.
Simulation shall be treated as a normal part of the workflow for cases that already rely on it.
Broader or still-evaluated uses of simulation shall remain tentative.
The simulator shall automatically assemble standard, repeatable pieces.
The simulator shall automatically pull the selected stage defaults.
The simulator shall automatically pull the compatible error model set.

The simulator shall infer safe compatibility choices when the user has already provided the key goal of the run.

A person shall provide or verify special calibration assumptions.

The system shall treat the source or population definition as a required entity for a run.

The system shall treat extra metadata as optional.
The system shall treat convenience defaults that do not change the scientific meaning of the output as optional.
If a needed entity is missing, the simulator shall fail fast and tell the user exactly what is missing.

The system shall accept harmless convenience defaults with a warning.

Minor differences are acceptable only if they are purely non-scientific.
Minor differences such as ordering that does not affect interpretation are acceptable.
Minor differences such as metadata timestamps are acceptable.
Minor differences such as formatting that does not change the content are acceptable.
Anything that could alter a downstream result or break reproducibility shall be treated as a failure in that mode.
Anything that changes the scientific interpretation has to be fixed now.
Anything that breaks reproducibility has to be fixed now.
Anything that prevents comparison against reference Gaia processing has to be fixed now.
An issue that is understood and bounded can be recorded as an exception for this release if users can still validate safely with a documented caveat.
An issue that only affects completeness can wait for a later release.
An issue that only affects convenience can wait for a later release.
An issue that only affects a non-critical edge case can wait for a later release.
If the current Gaia assets cannot be consumed or produced without the conversion, the conversion must be done now.
If the data can still move through the workflow with a reliable, documented workaround that users are willing to accept for the first release, the conversion can be deferred.
If the mismatch would only affect a future cleanup or a nicer integration path, the conversion can wait for a later migration step.
The deciding criterion is whether the format issue blocks the core simulator workflow or only makes it less elegant.
When a scientific model is updated, the new behavior shall be introduced in a controlled release.

The system shall support using a shortcut to test or validate a specific processing stage.
The system shall support using a shortcut to generate large representative datasets quickly without requiring the earlier mission systems to be faithful.

If the traceability chain cannot be reconstructed, the output should not be treated as fully auditable for comparison or reproduction.
If both the historical form and the canonical form are useful, the system shall store both and treat the original as the source of truth.
